title: Graduate Partnership Executive
description: <p></p> <p><strong>About us</strong></p> <p>Fospha is the measurement system enterprise retail and ecommerce brands run their business on. We give marketing teams one clear, daily view of what's actually working — across every channel and everywhere they sell, from their website to Amazon and TikTok Shop — down to the level of a single ad or piece of creative. It replaces guesswork and gut feel with a number marketing, finance and agencies can all trust and act on. Brands including Dyson, Gymshark, Lululemon and many more use Fospha up to 25 times a day to decide where budget should move next. We've spent over a decade building this, with more than $40 billion in marketing spend now optimised through the platform - and we're scaling fast across London, Mumbai and Austin.</p> <p><strong>The Graduate Opportunity at Fospha</strong></p> <p>Joining Fospha’s graduate programme means stepping into a fast-paced environment where you’ll gain real responsibility and exposure from day one. In Partnerships, graduates work directly with some of the world’s biggest digital platforms - like TikTok, Meta, and Snapchat - playing a key role in strengthening relationships, enabling joint initiatives, and driving partner success.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Hands-on exposure to our Partnerships:</strong> Working directly with the platforms such as Tiktok, Meta and Snap, you will build commercial acumen, develop strategic communication skills, and gain a deep understanding of how the digital advertising ecosystem works.</li> <li><strong>Cross-Functional Exposure</strong>: With support, cross-functional collaboration, and the opportunity to make a visible impact early on, it’s the ideal launchpad for ambitious graduates looking to break into the world of ad tech and strategic partnerships.</li> <li><strong>Comprehensive Training</strong>: In addition to the extensive on-the-job learning opportunities, you'll receive a broad and blended in-person training curriculum covering essential topics such as Business Storytelling, Relationship Building, Market Research & Product and Financial Management.</li> </ul> <p><strong>The Role:</strong></p> <p>As a <strong>Partnerships Executive</strong>, you'll join a high-impact team focused on enabling, scaling, and deepening Fospha’s relationships with the platforms that power digital marketing.</p> <p>This is a graduate-level role designed to develop future leaders. You’ll be hands-on with major ad platforms, supporting both strategic execution and day-to-day coordination. You’ll also work closely with internal teams - especially Marketing, Product and our Customer Teams - to make sure our partners have what they need to help customers grow.</p> <p><strong>Key responsibilities:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Supporting our partner managers in coordinating with Google, Meta, TikTok, Snap and others</li> <li>Preparing decks, talking points and training sessions to enable partner sales teams</li> <li>Tracking and reporting on partner performance and engagement</li> <li>Liaising across internal teams to keep initiatives moving and aligned</li> <li>Owning communications or enablement efforts for specific territories or smaller partners</li> <li>Researching and initiating contact with emerging or long-tail partners</li> <li>In addition to your core responsibilities, we expect you to be excited by the opportunity Gen AI brings and find new ways of working utilising our Gen Ai hub!</li> </ul> <p><strong>What are we looking for?</strong></p> <p>We hire for potential – you don’t need a technical degree or marketing background. You should apply if you:</p> <ul> <li>Are an excellent communicator – written, verbal, and visual</li> <li>Are highly organised and detail-oriented</li> <li>Are curious about how marketing, measurement and partnerships work</li> <li>Can handle multiple workstreams and work well under light-touch supervision</li> <li>Thrive in fast-moving, high-growth environments</li> <li>Want to make a real commercial impact from day one</li> </ul> <p><strong>Bonus Points For:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience with TikTok Ads, Meta, or other digital marketing tools</li> <li>Familiarity with platforms like Notion, HubSpot, Google Sheets</li> <li>Any internship or part-time experience in partnerships, sales, marketing or client-facing roles</li> <li>Like shopping and are a customer of retail brands</li> </ul> <p><strong>Our Values and Principles</strong></p> <p>You will be able to demonstrate examples of our core principles:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Seek inclusion & diversity:</strong> We create an environment where everyone feels welcome, and people are encouraged to speak and be heard</li> <li><strong>Work Hard, Work Well, Work Together:</strong> We take responsibility for making things happen, independently and together; we help colleagues in need and close loops, making sure our work is complete and has lasting impact</li> <li><strong>Grow</strong>: We are proactive, curious and unafraid of failure</li> <li><strong>Customer at the heart</strong>: We care about the customer, feel their pain and love building product that solves their biggest problems</li> <li><strong>Candour with caring:</strong> We deliver candid feedback with kindness and receive it with gratitude</li> </ul> <p><strong>What we can offer you</strong></p> <ul> <li>A workplace pension, through Royal London, with Fospha matching your contributions up to 3%</li> <li>A £1,000/year flexible benefits allowance to put towards private medical insurance, dental cover, a health cash plan, gym membership, extra holiday, or a pension top-up - whatever suits you!</li> <li>Access to Wellhub, giving you one membership across gyms, boutique studios, and wellbeing apps</li> <li>25 days' annual leave plus 8 UK bank holidays, an extra day off for your birthday! and more holiday the longer you stay (26 days after 3 years, 27 after 6)</li> <li>Life assurance worth 4x your annual salary, from day one</li> <li>Cycle to Work scheme, plus discounts on everyday spending through our benefits portal — Apple, Tesco, IKEA, M&S, Deliveroo, cinema tickets and more</li> <li>Quarterly one-to-one sessions with a financial adviser, plus access to payroll-deducted loans through Salary Finance</li> <li>Paid volunteering days each year</li> <li>Regular socials, free weekly snacks, and Lunch & Learn events at our Scale Space office, plus access to the wider Blenheim Chalcot community</li> <li>Opportunities to travel — including to our India and North America offices</li> </ul> <p><strong>The Process</strong></p> <ul> <li>5-10 minute screening call with a member of the Talent Team</li> <li>30-minute Team Screen interview</li> <li>Task and Panel interview</li> <li>Final Exec interview</li> </ul> <p><em>Top tip: Make sure to thoroughly research Fospha and tell us why you would be a great fit for the role!</em></p> <p></p><div class="content-conclusion"><p>By submitting title: Product Engineer
description: <p></p> <p><strong>ABOUT NEXGEN CLOUD</strong></p> <p>NexGen Cloud is a fast-growing GPU cloud and AI infrastructure business. We’re the company behind Hyperstack — a self-serve, on-demand cloud platform built for high-performance AI, HPC, and compute-heavy workloads. Powered by 100% renewable energy and NVIDIA architecture, Hyperstack gives teams from AI startups to enterprise the compute they need, without the cost or complexity of legacy cloud.</p> <p>We move fast, solve hard problems, and build things that matter. If you want ownership, real impact, and a front-row seat to one of the most consequential infrastructure shifts of the decade — this is the place.</p> <p><strong>THE ROLE: PRODUCT ENGINEER</strong></p> <p>Our hardest problems don’t stay in one layer. A customer issue can start in a web app and end in a Kubernetes scheduler, a container runtime or a GPU driver. We need engineers who can build the products, APIs and tools our customers use, and who understand the systems underneath well enough to make them work reliably in production.</p> <p>This is a role for someone who takes a loosely defined problem, works out what the user actually needs, and owns the solution end to end. That means designing it, writing the code, shipping it, and debugging it when it breaks, without handing it off at the first layer boundary.</p> <p><strong>WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING</strong></p> <p>Rather than a checklist, here’s what success in this role actually looks like:</p> <ul> <li>Own and drive user-facing products end to end, including web apps, APIs, backend services and CLI tools, mostly in Go. You’ll ship the simplest useful version first, then improve it based on how people actually use it.</li> <li>Collaborate closely with Product, Engineering & DevOps, Infrastructure & Data Centre Operations, Security and Customer Support. You’ll turn real customer problems into practical solutions.</li> <li>Build and maintain Kubernetes-based services, controllers and platform capabilities. This includes GPU scheduling and container runtimes.</li> <li>Identify repetitive operational work and replace it with automation, so software handles it instead of people.</li> <li>Investigate production issues across application code, Kubernetes, containers, Linux, networking, drivers and hardware. Each incident should end in a lasting fix, a guardrail or better tooling.</li> <li>Design services that behave well under load and during failure. You’ll instrument them so anyone can debug them, and give them secure defaults from day one.</li> <li>Contribute ideas and take ownership beyond your core remit. That includes product decisions on workflow and interface, such as whether a problem is best solved with a CLI, an API or a web experience.</li> </ul> <p><strong>ABOUT YOU</strong></p> <p>We care more about how you think and work than a perfect CV. You’ll likely bring a combination of the following:</p> <p><em>Essential:</em></p> <ul> <li>Strong professional experience building, debugging and operating production software in Go. Deep experience in another systems language also works, if you can show you’d become productive in Go quickly.</li> <li>Hands-on experience with Kubernetes and containers, including how workloads are scheduled, how services communicate, and how to investigate when things misbehave.</li> <li>Confidence in Linux environments: systemd, processes, signals, filesystems, permissions, networking, and CPU and memory diagnostics.</li> <li>A track record of systems, products or tools you personally designed and built.</li> <li>Solid engineering fundamentals: concurrency, API and interface design, and failure modes. You’ll also have practical experience troubleshooting production systems with logs, metrics and system-level tooling.</li> </ul> <p><em>Nice to Have:</em></p> <ul> <li>Familiarity with the NVIDIA GPU ecosystem, such as drivers, CUDA, nvidia-smi, GPU-enabled container runtimes or Kubernetes GPU scheduling. This isn’t essential: strong systems debugging and a genuine interest in learning this area count just as much.</li> <li>Experience with distributed and event-driven systems, such as queues, retries, idempotency and backpressure. Practical networking knowledge (DNS, TCP/IP, HTTP, load balancing) also helps.</li> <li>Experience building Kubernetes controllers or operators, or developer tooling used by other engineers. A security-minded approach to auth, secrets and attack surfaces is a plus.</li> </ul> <p><strong>WHAT WE OFFER</strong></p> <ul> <li>Competitive salary and annual discretionary bonus scheme</li> <li>Employee wellbeing benefits</li> <li>25 days holiday, plus public holidays</li> <li>Private Medical Insurance</li> <li>Enhanced Pension Scheme</li> <li>Flexible working arrangements (remote or hybrid, depending on role and location)</li> <li>Real ownership and autonomy — the trust to take initiative and experiment</li> <li>Visible, meaningful impact as we scale</li> <li>Clear career progression in a high-growth company</li> <li>A collaborative, international culture built on trust, transparency, and ownership</li> <li>The chance to help shape NexGen Cloud’s team, culture, and future</li> </ul> <p><strong>WHY APPLY</strong></p> <p>We welcome applications from all backgrounds. If you enjoy solving complex infrastructure problems and want to build something meaningful at scale, we’d like to hear from you.</p> <p><strong>MORE INFORMATION</strong></p> <p>Visit our <a href="https://www.nexgencloud.com/careers">careers page</a> to learn more about us or follow us on <a href="https://www.linkedin.com/company/nexgen-cloud">LinkedIn</a> and <a href="https://x.com/CloudNexgen">X</a> to learn more about our journey and keep up with our latest news and releases.</p> <p></p> Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Account Executive - Czech or Hungarian Speaker
description: <div class="content-intro"><p><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><strong>Our Mission: Why Lighthouse? </strong></span></p> <p><span style="font-size: 12pt;">At Lighthouse, we’re on a mission to revolutionize commercial strategy as hospitality’s most powerful AI platform. We take the world's largest hotel data network and transform it into real-time intelligence that drives action. We don't just deliver insights; we empower businesses to make decisions that move revenue. </span></p> <p><span style="font-size: 12pt;">With $370M in Series C funding and over $100M in ARR, we are scaling at lightspeed. Our 850+ teammates across 35 countries aren't just building software—they are leveraging cutting-edge AI to help hoteliers be the first to act. Tens of thousands of hotels across 185 countries trust Lighthouse to execute their commercial strategy, including every one of the top 15 global chains and thousands of independent hotels that consistently outperform their markets. With Lighthouse AI, the intelligence gets deeper. Decisions get smarter. Actions get faster. We help hoteliers be first to act.</span></p> <p><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><strong>Lighthouse Values: Our guiding light</strong></span></p> <p><span style="font-size: 12pt;">We are <strong><span style="color: rgb(253, 130, 55);">Lumineers</span></strong>. Our shared values keep us on a collaborative path fostering a cultural and customer centric environment</span></p> <ul> <li style="font-size: 12pt;"><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><span style="color: rgb(253, 130, 55);"><strong>Pursuit of greatness</strong></span>: We’re innovators who care deeply about our customers’ success. Our team brings their best work, stays curious, and delivers excellence through attention to detail</span></li> <li style="font-size: 12pt;"><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><span style="color: rgb(253, 130, 55);"><strong>Meaningful work matters</strong></span>: We make every moment count by knowing what to deliver, why it matters, and how it drives Lighthouse forward</span></li> <li style="font-size: 12pt;"><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><span style="color: rgb(253, 130, 55);"><strong>Elevate each other</strong></span>: We don’t just work together - we grow together. What unites us is understanding each other as people and working toward shared goals</span></li> </ul> <p><span style="font-size: 12pt;">We’re more than just a workplace – we’re a community. Collaborative, fun, and deeply committed, we work hard together to revolutionize the hospitality sector. Are you ready to join us and shine brighter in the industry’s most exciting rocket-ship? 🚀</span></p></div><p><span style="font-size: 12pt; font-family: helvetica, arial, sans-serif;"><strong>Job Details</strong></span></p> <ul> <li style="font-size: 12pt; font-family: helvetica, arial, sans-serif;"><span style="font-size: 12pt; font-family: helvetica, arial, sans-serif;">💼 Revenue </span></li> <li style="font-size: 12pt; font-family: helvetica, arial, sans-serif;"><span style="font-size: 12pt; font-family: helvetica, arial, sans-serif;">📍 United Kingdom</span></li> <li style="font-size: 12pt; font-family: helvetica, arial, sans-serif;"><span style="font-size: 12pt; font-family: helvetica, arial, sans-serif;">🕜 Full-Time/Remote </span></li> </ul> <p><span style="font-size: 12pt; font-family: helvetica, arial, sans-serif;"><strong>What you will do</strong></span></p> <p><span style="font-size: 12pt;">You’ll be the face of Lighthouse for new customers, owning the full sales cycle from first cold touch to close. This is a hunter role: you carry a quota, you build your own pipeline, and you’re accountable to outcomes and success. No excuses, just results. </span></p> <p><span style="font-size: 12pt;">Your market is two-sided. You open net-new accounts that fit our ideal customer profile and have never spoken to us, and you turn low-adoption customers who use a single Lighthouse product into full-platform customers. In both cases the goal is the same: the whole commercial platform, not one module. Small, one-off transactions are not what this role is for. You think in terms of the full deal from the first conversation, and you have the patience and the process to run a complex, multi-stakeholder cycle to get there. </span></p> <p><span style="font-size: 12pt;">What makes this different: you won’t do it alone. Lighthouse is deploying an agent AI infrastructure — Enablement, Pre-Sales, and Coaching agents — alongside a modern revenue stack. AI handles the prep, the sequencing, and the pattern recognition so you can focus on what matters — building relationships, running sharp discovery, and closing deals.</span></p> <p><span style="font-size: 12pt; font-family: helvetica, arial, sans-serif;"><strong>Where you will have impact</strong></span></p> <p><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><strong>Own your territory and your number. </strong>Build and execute a strategic territory plan to generate a net-new pipeline. Maintain 3x pipeline coverage, forecast honestly, and take full accountability for your results. Your quota is your commitment. </span></p> <p><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><strong>Hunt into net-new accounts. </strong>Cold, outbound prospecting into ideal customer profile accounts is the core of this role, not a supplement to inbound. Run an AI-first workflow: use our agents for account research, buying signals, sequencing and first-touch personalization, so your time goes into conversations rather than admin. Add Lighthouse Connect events and industry conferences on top. This is not an SDR-reliant role. </span></p> <p><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><strong>Expand low-adoption customers. </strong>Identify customers who use a single Lighthouse product, or a fraction of what they bought, and turn them into full-platform accounts. Run this as a sales cycle, with discovery, a business case and a close, not as an adoption program. Work with Customer Success on the handover so the account is set up to keep growing. </span></p> <p><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><strong>Turn small deals into big deals. </strong>Treat every opportunity as a platform deal. Qualify for the full scope early, bring in every stakeholder who has a say, and build the business case for the whole solution rather than settling for a trial or a single module. Protect pricing on value. </span></p> <p><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><strong>Run a disciplined sales process. </strong>Using MEDDPICC to qualify and advance opportunities. Use the AI Pre-Sales Agent to identify gaps before every major call. Advance deals through stage gates with evidence, not optimism. Leverage AI to make your days easier and focus on more selling time. </span></p> <p><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><strong>Use AI as a force multiplier. </strong>Leverage the Enablement Agent for call prep, discovery frameworks, and positioning. Use the Coaching Agent to surface patterns in your pipeline and win rate. Push back on the tools when they’re wrong — help make the system smarter. </span></p> <p><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><strong>Become a hospitality expert. </strong>Understand the commercial challenges hotels face across pricing, distribution, and business intelligence. Position Lighthouse’s full platform as the integrated solution that replaces fragmented point tools. Know the competitive landscape inside out and run value based ROI conversations confidently. </span></p> <p><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><strong>Build relationships at a distance. </strong>Most of your buyers will never meet you in person. Earn trust over video, phone and email through sharp preparation, clear follow-through and a point of view on their business. Partner with Product to share market feedback and influence the roadmap, and represent Lighthouse at industry events to build the brand and your network. </span></p> <p><span style="font-size: 12pt; font-family: helvetica, arial, sans-serif;"><strong>About our team</strong></span></p> <p><span style="font-size: 12pt; font-family: helvetica, arial, sans-serif;">You’ll join a global Revenue team of 150+ sales professionals across 24 countries. The Acquisition team is where new revenue starts: we open the accounts the rest of the company grows. We work across the full Lighthouse product suite, helping hotels, chains, and hospitality groups achieve their commercial goals. It’s a collaborative, high-energy environment that celebrates wins loudly, with real opportunities for career growth and the chance to learn from experienced leaders.</span></p> <p><span style="font-size: 12pt; font-family: helvetica, arial, sans-serif;"><strong>What's in it for you?</strong></span></p> <ul> <li style="font-size: 12pt;"><span style="font-size: 12pt;">Flexible working environment: Work from home or at one of our global offices.</span></li> <li style="font-size: 12pt;"><span style="font-size: 12pt;">Comprehensive health insurance: Private AXA coverage for you and your family.</span></li> <li style="font-size: 12pt;"><span style="font-size: 12pt;">Flexible time off: Autonomy to manage your work-life balance.</span></li> <li style="font-size: 12pt;"><span style="font-size: 12pt;">Competitive compensation: Proactively maintained to value your work.</span></li> <li style="font-size: 12pt;"><span style="font-size: 12pt;">Collaborative team: High-bar, friendly, creative, and passionate colleagues.</span></li> <li style="font-size: 12pt;"><span style="font-size: 12pt;">Career development: Workshops and frameworks to realize your full potential.</span></li> <li style="font-size: 12pt;"><span style="font-size: 12pt;">Impactful work: Shape products relied on by 85,000+ users worldwide.</span></li> <li style="font-size: 12pt;"><span style="font-size: 12pt;">Wellbeing support: Subsidized up to 80% ClassPass subscription.</span></li> <li style="font-size: 12pt;"><span style="font-size: 12pt;">Referral bonuses: Earn rewards for bringing in new talent.</span></li> <li style="font-size: 12pt;"><span style="font-size: 12pt;">Additional maternity leave compensation: For the first 12 weeks of Statutory Maternity Pay (SMP), we top-up your SMP so that your salary reaches 100%</span></li> </ul> <p><span style="font-size: 12pt; font-family: helvetica, arial, sans-serif;"><strong>Who you are</strong></span></p> <ul> <li style="font-size: 12pt;"><span style="font-size: 12pt;">2–5 years in a closing sales role, SaaS experience is a must but hunger and skill matters more than industry tenure. </span></li> <li style="font-size: 12pt;"><span style="font-size: 12pt;">A hunter by instinct. title: Senior Quality Systems Engineer, United Kingdom
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.</p></div><h3><strong>About the Team</strong></h3> <p>Anduril’s Quality organization is seeking a Quality Systems Engineer to join our London team and help develop future opportunities for our internal quality management system and digitization efforts. The Quality team works with our customers, internal teams, and suppliers to ensure the deployment of reliable products that meet all mission requirements. We develop cutting-edge Quality processes and methods to secure scalable, long-term business success.<br>We are growing and this role will focus on internal site growth and implementing a world-class quality management system, supporting our internal manufacturing sites, supplier sites, and allied facilities. This role carries responsibility for ensuring compliance with UK and European regulatory frameworks, NATO Standardization Agreements (STANAGs) for aerospace, and UK Ministry of Defense (MOD) requirements as part of our London operations.<br>The right person for this role has extensive knowledge in Quality Management System (QMS) systems, data analysis, and continuous improvement to help shape our internal systems, tools, procedures and the culture of quality at Anduril. If you are someone who loves to build world-class Quality processes, work hands-on, help others succeed on the quality journey, and be accountable for results, then this role is for you.</p> <h3><strong>About the Job</strong></h3> <p>Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a real time, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.<br><br></p> <p><strong>What You’ll Do</strong></p> <ul> <li>Develop, lead, and manage the execution of the QMS and its top-level processes. Coordinate resources and prioritization of tasks to complete internal and external audits of the QMS.</li> <li>Develop, lead, and manage the execution of the QMS software implementation and adoption across Anduril sites, including the London facility. Coordinate resources and prioritization of tasks to complete implementation, internal and external audits of the QMS.</li> <li>Ensure full compliance with UK regulatory requirements, including UK MOD Defense Standards (DEF STANs), UKCA marking where applicable, and relevant UK Health & Safety Executive (HSE) regulations for defense manufacturing environments.</li> <li>Drive compliance with NATO Standardization Agreements (STANAGs) for aerospace quality, including STANAG 4107 (Mutual Acceptance of Government Quality Assurance and Usage of the Allied Quality Assurance Publications), STANAG 4159 (NATO Quality Assurance Requirements for Design, Development and Production — AQAP-2110), and STANAG 4161 (NATO Quality Management System Requirements for Aviation, Space and Defense — AQAP-2310).</li> <li>Ensure conformance to STANAG 4404 and associated AQAPs for software-intensive aerospace systems, including AQAP-2210 (NATO Supplementary Software Quality Assurance Requirements) as applicable to Lattice OS and embedded mission systems.</li> <li>Support implementation of STANAG 4685 (Airworthiness) requirements as they relate to quality assurance processes for unmanned aerial systems and aerospace components.</li> <li>Liaise with the UK MOD Quality Assurance representatives, the Defence Quality Assurance (DQA) organisation, and NATO Quality Assurance authorities to support Government Quality Assurance (GQA) activities and audits.</li> <li>Partner with business systems team, product quality engineers and manufacturing engineers to help prepare new processes, digital tools, and sites to meet QMS requirements, develop new capabilities to meet existing QMS requirements and conduct internal audits before manufacturing readiness review and production readiness review.</li> <li>Develop our internal QMS road map for tools and capabilities to match the scaling of the company: to meet customer needs, to enable quality capabilities for new products, and scale quality processes as we grow — with particular attention to UK Export Control and ITAR/EAR interface requirements.</li> <li>Ensure compliance with UK data protection requirements (UK GDPR / Data Protection Act 2018) as they relate to quality records, supplier data, and audit documentation.</li> <li>Become a systems expert for Anduril’s quality tools, processes, and data sets to enable effective QMS execution across both US and UK operations.</li> <li>Communicate with external audit agencies, including UKAS-accredited certification bodies and NATO quality assurance authorities. Support customer audits as necessary.</li> <li>Manage the QMS internal audit program and lead internal audits.</li> <li>Identify and implement continuous improvement opportunities that benefit the QMS and product quality, aligned with AS9100, NATO AQAP, and STANAG frameworks.</li> <li>Support investigations, initiatives, and projects as needed, at the team or organisation level.</li> <li>Support developing QMS training modules and packages, including UK/NATO-specific regulatory and STANAG training. Facilitate training records and retention with manager of affected trainees.</li> <li>Drive root cause analysis and corrective action with internal findings from audits and customer visits, including UK MOD and NATO audit findings.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Required Qualifications</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree and 3–5 years of experience in aerospace and/or defence manufacturing.</li> <li>Expert knowledge of QMS requirements and auditing in a complex product environment, in one or more of the following QMS standards: ISO 9001:2015, AS9100D, AS9110C, AS9120B, AS6500, IATF 16949:2016, ISO 13485:2016, TL 9000 R6.3.</li> <li>Demonstrable knowledge of NATO Standardization Agreements (STANAGs) for aerospace quality, including STANAG 4107, STANAG 4159, STANAG 4161, and their associated Allied Quality Assurance Publications (AQAPs): AQAP-2110, AQAP-2210, and AQAP-2310.</li> <li>Familiarity with UK MOD Defence Standards (DEF STANs) and Government Quality Assurance (GQA) processes.</li> <li>Understanding of UK regulatory frameworks relevant to defence manufacturing, including UK Export Control Act 2002, HSE regulations, and UKCA/CE marking requirements.</li> <li>Working knowledge with QMS software solutions which might include Net Inspect, Siemens, SAP, ETQ, One Factory, MasterControl, Compliance Quest, Hexagon, PTC, QT9.</li> <li>Hands-on experience with data analytics platforms, reporting tools, and basic data visualisation.</li> <li>Demonstrated project management for software system implementation and onboarding suppliers (external users) and internal users.</li> <li>Working knowledge of design, development, manufacturing, supply chain, deployment, contracts, and other organisations that are part of a company-wide audit.</li> <li>Knowledge Here, you're on the whiteboard at ideation, so compliant by design is the plan, not the clean-up. And the stakes are real. Taptap Send moves billions of dollars every month across 100 countries, and is now building wallets, cards and broader financial products for diaspora communities. The job You'll advise on new licensing and products from first idea to go-live, and own regulator engagement across our markets. Shape products before they're built: review designs, UX, flows and terms against regulatory and customer-outcome rules, Consumer Duty included, while change is still cheap. Turn regulation into decisions: what's mandatory, what's prudent, and the alternative route that still gets it launched. Own the regulator relationship: across our markets, including new ones, and flag what regulatory change means for the roadmap early. Take products to new countries: localise what already works, with country leads and local counsel. Build the playbooks: templates that let Legal scale without adding friction. Why you'll want it Spend your time on the hard questions. You're asked to shape our roadmap and launches, and understand how to fit them to the relevant regimes Be a peer, with room to run. You'll join a flat team of regulatory and commercial lawyers, with real autonomy and a manager who trusts you. Make launches faster, not slower. Legal in the room from day one is how products here ship sooner. That's the whole point of your seat. Make sending money home cheaper. Remittances pay for school fees, rent and medical bills, and are worth more than all foreign aid combined. Cheaper, reliable transfers put more of that money in families' hands. Is this you? You're a qualified lawyer (UK or equivalent) with 4+ years' PQE in payments, e-money or financial services regulation, at a firm, a regulator or a fintech. You've advised payments or e-money firms under the FCA or an equivalent regime, dealt with the regulator directly, and helped product teams take live launches over the line. You give the answer first and the reasoning second. Ambiguity across several jurisdictions doesn't stop you making the call. If you'd rather be asked first than asked last, apply. title: Analytics Engineer
description: Tired of being told “that’s not your scope”? Plenty of good analysts hit the same wall: you query the data but never build the pipelines, you’re boxed into one lane, and more scope means waiting your turn. Here, it’s the opposite. Taptap Send moves billions of dollars a month across 6 of 7 continents . We’re probably the largest, fastest-growing money movement business you’ve never heard of. Cards, wallets, business-to-business payments, institutional payments, and new markets are all launching now, and each needs its data, reconciliations and reporting built from scratch. That’s your work. The job You’ll own the external reports the business can’t operate without, then automate them into reliable, reusable dbt models. From day one you’ll work with Finance, Compliance, Treasury, Product and Data Engineering to make sure every number is modelled correctly. Own external reporting: deliver the datasets behind month-end close and regulatory reporting, on time, every cycle. Automate: turn multi-day manual work into scheduled pipelines, runbooks and dbt models, so it only gets done once. Get ahead of launches: build reports and reconciliations as each product and market goes live, before anyone asks. Be first line for data requests: build models so people and AI agents can answer repeat questions themselves. Keep data trustworthy: build tests, checks and alerts that catch reconciliation breaks and stale data before they become incidents. Share what you know: peer-review code and join our weekly meetups. Why you’ll want it Grow as fast as you’re able. We hire for potential, not years of experience. On a lean, talent-dense team, you’ll own real work early and take on more the moment you’re ready. Go from querying data to designing systems. Data, product or business analyst? You don’t need to be an analytics engineer yet. Build the pipelines behind the numbers, and learn dbt, testing, automation and AI tooling from senior analytics engineers. Don't get boxed in. Own the reporting, automate it, then take on our biggest problems wherever they sit. Your hiring manager started in Finance and has since worked across Partner Ops, Fraud, Compliance, Reconciliation and Product. See the whole business. You’ll follow a transfer from the moment a customer taps send, through partner payout and reconciliation, to the report a regulator reads. Own numbers that matter. Auditors and Finance rely on what you build. This isn’t a dashboard role. Put more money in families’ hands. Remittances are a lifeline for millions of families and are worth more than all foreign aid. Every report you automate helps us keep transfers cheap and reliable. You’ll fit if you have 1-2+ years in a data or analytics role A technical or quantitative degree, or equivalent experience Strong SQL and experience wrangling messy, complex data Some experience automating repetitive work (e.g. scripts, scheduled jobs) A strong sense of ownership: when something is broken, ownerless or late, you step in, fix it, and make sure it doesn’t happen again Reliability under deadlines, a “no task too small” attitude, and comfort chasing stakeholders The right to work in the UK Nice to have: startup or scale-up experience, Python or R, dbt, Looker or Mode, and something you’ve built, at work or on the side, because the manual way annoyed you. title: Head of India
description: The Role India is the biggest remittance market with over $130 billion a year flowing home to it, from everywhere: engineers in the Bay Area and Sydney, cabbies in Toronto, construction crews in Dubai, shopkeepers in Leicester, students in Berlin. From Punjabis, Gujaratis, Tamils, Malayalis and Telugus. From people wiring $3,000 a month to a Mumbai mortgage and people sending $80 to a village in Bihar. Your job is to win this market. You are someone who gets excited by the nuances of the Indian diaspora and how to reach each group, and who wants to own the P&L, the regulatory landscape and pricing at the same time. If you find the price sensitivity of each cohort exciting, and "why do Malayali nurses cluster in specific hospital systems, and what does that mean for acquisition?" as interesting as "what's RBI's latest remittance policy and which banks make the best partners," this is it. As the GM, you own the P&L, and set pricing. For customer growth, you decide which communities to acquire and in what order. Know the RBI's rules well enough to see the openings inside them, not just the limits. A Gujarati family in New Jersey and a Punjabi trucker in Brampton got abroad through completely different networks, and reaching them takes completely different channels. Reports to the Head of South Asia. Builds a team of FX Advisors in India and growth managers in sending markets. The face of India inside and outside the company. Total ownership. Be your own CEO What You'll Own The P&L. Volume, gross profit and CAC across every India corridor. Not influence, own. A miss is your miss. A beat is your win. Strategy and sequencing. Which sender markets, which communities, which channels, in what order. US, Canada, UK, Europe, Australia and UAE to start. Build the plan, defend it to leadership, execute it. Pricing. India is the most rate-sensitive, most competitive remittance market in the world, up against competitors who reprice daily. Set FX and fee strategy corridor by corridor. The regulatory and partner landscape. RBI rules, bank partnerships, payout rails. Know the terrain cold and own the local relationships. Product. Obsess over UX and the services NRIs actually need. Closer to the customer than anyone in the company, and what you hear feeds straight into product, pricing and customer support. The diaspora puzzle. Community partnerships, temples and gurdwaras and churches, cricket leagues, student associations, remittance-heavy employers, influencers, festivals (Diwali is a season, not a day). Get in front of each community authentically, and cheaply. The team. Hire, coach and retain people in India and in sending markets. Small, dense, fast. Who You Are 10 to 15 years in high-growth environments: startups, operations, consulting, finance, fintech. Has owned a number and talks about it the way owners do. Diaspora-fluent. Real knowledge of and networks in the Indian diaspora, and real curiosity about it. Migration patterns, community structures, who sends money to whom and why. Commercially sharp. Holds pricing, unit economics and CAC math in their head, and works the data directly. Excel or Sheets required, SQL a real plus. A hustler with judgment. Closes a bank partnership Monday, reviews corridor margins Tuesday, shows up at a community event in Jackson Heights on Saturday. Likes all three. A regulatory realist. Understands (or can quickly master) RBI rules and the compliance realities of moving money into India. Treats compliance as a partner, not an obstacle. Multilingual, ideally. Fluent in English. Hindi, Gujarati, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu or Malayalam are genuine assets. Location: London or Dubai. Regular travel to India and sending markets is part of the job. Why This Role India is the largest remittance market in the world, and winning it moves the whole company forward. This role owns that outcome, with the authority and the accountability that come with it. It also drives real value for the customers: Immigrants work hard for this money, and every basis point saved goes home. This is unsecured personal lending in the higher-APR mid-prime space (30% to 50% APR), with loans typically from £2,000 to £10,000, and customers acquired primarily through price-comparison and aggregator marketplaces. Our ambition is to grow this product many times over while improving its economics, and this role owns the product that makes that happen. This is a product role first. You will own the Express/Mid-prime proposition end to end: who we serve, how we quote and present offers on marketplaces, how the journey converts, how we price, and how the product performs once the loans are on the book. What makes it different from a typical product role is that the product is credit. The levers that drive growth, such as eligibility, pricing, offer design and underwriting, are the same levers that drive loss rates, so you need to be comfortable working with risk and data science rather than handing that part off. We think this is a great role for someone with around four to five years of experience who has built a strong foundation in lending or fintech, has worked hands-on with data and credit decisioning, and is ready to own a product outright rather than a slice of one. You will set the direction for the segment, run the roadmap, and be accountable for the results, with the backing of experienced risk, data science and commercial leaders around you. Our decisioning is built on Open Banking and cashflow underwriting rather than credit scores alone. For a higher-APR population acquired through marketplaces, seeing real affordability is what lets us select and price better than the market. The interesting product problem is that richer data comes at a cost to conversion, so the job is to capture that data advantage while designing a journey and offer that customers actually complete. The defining challenge is balance: scaling volume by an order of magnitude while building a book of genuinely good credit quality. title: Project Engineer (Data Centres & Industrials)
description: About the role Octopus is building a new business line delivering low-cost, reliable, clean energy and faster speed-to-power for data centres and large industrials. We're looking for a Project Electrical Engineer to be the electrical owner on first-of-a-kind power projects - private wire, behind-the-meter generation and storage, MV and HV grid connections. This is a technical role with a unique expanded scope to broader infrastructure project management. Early on you are the project manager: you hold the programme, the development budget and the external parties, from concept design through connection offer to design freeze and financial close. From there you stay on as the electrical owner through construction, commissioning and energisation, with a delivery team around you. What you'll do Own the programme and the development budget. Schedule from early concept to design freeze - siting, connection application, planning, consents, procurement, long-lead items - worked back from the customer's energisation date. Appoint and manage consultants, ICPs and study providers. Surface risk early and clearly communicate them to the stakeholders. Own the electrical concept through to sign-off. Single-line diagrams, general arrangements, switchgear and plant layouts, cable routes, metering and comms architecture. Direct and interrogate the studies (load flow, short-circuit, protection coordination, arc flash, earthing, power quality). Chair design reviews and stage gates, and take options to the Project Lead and customer with a recommendation. Lead the grid interface. DNO, TO and NESO - applications and offers, technical requirements, securities and milestones, contestable and non-contestable scope, ICP/IDNO coordination, MPAN registration. Budget ownership through completion. Credible capex inputs for the project model across plant, substation, civils and enabling works, with value engineering and optioneering. Then FAT/SAT witnessing, commissioning plans and sequences of operation, energisation and handover. Take on what you haven't done before. First-of-a-kind means no precedent, no standard design and no colleague who's done it. Get to a working understanding of an unfamiliar technology or scope fast, and deliver it. What you'll have Master’s degree, or equivalent, in electrical or power systems engineering. CEng welcome, not essential. 5+ years delivering energy or infrastructure projects, with a strong grounding in MV and HV systems. Real infrastructure experience - substations, networks, industrial plant, data centres, utilities, water or transport. We care that you've dealt with ground conditions, easements, consents, tie-ins to live assets and construction sequencing. This is not a grid-only role. You've personally held a programme and a budget on a development or pre-construction project. A GB/European grid connection taken from connection offer to grid code compliance and energisation, with working knowledge of the Grid Code, CUSC, SQSS, G99/G100, ENA engineering recommendations and BS 7671. Able to coordinate a multi-discipline design where you're not the expert in every discipline - and to spot a weak answer from a civil or mechanical engineer. Comfortable as the single point of accountability with an incomplete picture, holding external parties accountable without formal authority. Full UK driving licence and willing to travel to site. It would be great if you have... BESS, private wire, microgrid or behind-the-meter generation; data centre or mission-critical power (MV/LV distribution, UPS, generators, redundancy topologies, commissioning levels); study tools (ETAP, PowerFactory, IPSA, PSS/E, PSCAD) or Python; IEC 61850, Modbus, DNP3, SCADA and metering data flows; NEC or FIDIC contract and change management. Project management credentials (APM, PRINCE2, MS Project, Primavera) - though we care far more about what you've delivered. Why else you'll love it here • Wondering what the salary for this role is? title: (Senior) Data Systems Lead
description: Help us make a big green dent in the universe. We're on a mission to drive the global renewable energy revolution, and we need many more people to help us make our vision a reality. Octopus Energy Generation (OEGEN) is a leader in sourcing, investing in, and managing a wide range of utility-scale renewable energy assets. As we continue to expand our investment base, we are dedicated to building a diverse team that reflects the communities we serve. Currently, we manage a global portfolio of over £8 billion in renewable energy assets. We are committed to delivering best-in-class responsible investment activity, offering like-minded investors the means and products to invest their capital sustainably. It is our ambition to change the entire energy lifecycle and make every green electron matter, delivering the best outcomes for customers, investors, the environment and society, accelerating the transition to net zero. OEGEN Data, Tech & Transformation Team We are embarking on a comprehensive transformation program designed to drive significant advancements in our business operations and technology landscape. Our primary goal is to transition from our current reliance on legacy systems and specialized off-the-shelf tools to a more integrated, AI-driven, and data-centric operational model. Leveraging insights and guidance from our other technically mature entities like Kraken and OE, we plan to adopt cutting-edge tools and capabilities, particularly in AI and Python-driven solutions. By investing in a diverse range of skills, we aim to create a hybrid team capable of operating in both our legacy and future environments, ultimately transforming OEGEN into an efficient, data-driven organization. About the role The tools are already here. Like the rest of OE Group, OEGEN runs on Databricks, we're moving onto our own Microsoft 365 tenant, and Octopus Energy Group gives us access to a powerful set of shared data and AI capabilities. What we're missing is someone whose job is to make all of it work together for our Fund Management business - and then build genuinely useful things on top of it. This is a two-sided role. On one side, you'll integrate: wiring third-party systems, internal apps and document storage into the environment we already have, setting sensible guardrails around access and cost, and adopting existing Group capability wherever it does the job rather than rebuilding it. On the other, you'll build: turning those connections into data products, internal tools and AI-enabled workflows that fund management, asset management and finance use every day. Tying the two together, you'll develop and own the playbook - the documented, repeatable patterns for how a new system gets connected, how a tool gets built and shipped, and how both get supported afterwards - so that what you learn once becomes how the whole team works. The two halves feed each other: you'll understand what's possible because you built the plumbing, and you'll build better plumbing because you know what people actually do with it. We want someone with genuine ideas about where AI can take a business like ours, and the pragmatism to ship them. Our team has already built an Excel data mart plugin that puts gold-layer tables directly in the hands of non-technical staff, a metrics taxonomy app that keeps third-party definitions aligned with our own, and AI-assisted workflows that scaffold documentation automatically. There's a long list of things we haven't got to yet. Expect roughly half your time on integration and enablement and half on building, and expect to work closely with the central data platform team so what we do in OEGEN stays consistent with the wider estate and our specific needs get onto their roadmap. What You'll Do Integrate the systems our business runs on - third-party providers, internal tools, our own SharePoint and Microsoft 365 tenant - into our existing Databricks environment, via APIs and existing connectors. Build data products on top of what you connect: well-modelled, documented, reusable datasets that the business consumes directly through Excel, dashboards and natural-language querying, rather than one-off extracts. Design and ship internal applications and AI-enabled tools - using Python, Streamlit , Databricks Apps (HTMX) , Lakebase , FastAPI or similar - that put data and AI directly into the hands of fund management, asset management and finance teams. Prototype, evaluate and productionise new AI capability, from document AI and retrieval to agentic workflows, and turn the ideas that prove out into supported products rather than abandoned experiments. Take an adopt-first approach: work with Octopus Energy Group's data platform and AI teams to reuse capability that already exists, and configure it for OEGEN rather than building parallel versions of it. Set up practical guardrails inside Databricks and Unity Catalog - schema and workspace access, permissions, environment hygiene - so more teams can use it without stepping on each other. Bring cost management from reactive to proactive: tagging, budgets, alerting and usage monitoring, so Databricks and AI token spend can be attributed to the right team, project or fund before the invoice arrives. Get our AI usage properly credentialed and logged - managed keys and access rather than API keys sitting in individual password managers - and provide clean patterns for embedding AI into the tools we build. Standardise how we build and ship internal apps: shared templates, authentication, deployment and documentation, so a tool remains supportable by someone other than the person who wrote it. Consolidate the ad-hoc scripts, spreadsheets and no-code workflows we've accumulated into fewer, better-understood integrations that don't need babysitting, and automate the repetitive parts of our own workflow. Work directly with non-technical teams to understand their problems and translate them into things we can build. What You'll Need Strong systems integration experience - connecting business systems, SaaS tools and data sources via REST APIs, connectors and authentication flows. A track record of building and shipping data products or internal applications that people actually use , not just pipelines that feed someone else's reports. Solid Python and SQL, used daily for building, automation and data modelling . Hands-on experience with a cloud data platform in production (Databricks preferred): workspaces, catalogs, permissions and compute . Practical experience integrating AI into real tools - LLM APIs, retrieval, agents - with a clear-eyed sense of what works and what's still a demo. Practical identity and access experience - SSO, service accounts, credential management and access lifecycle - enough to make sensible, secure choices without a security team holding your hand. Experience with Microsoft 365 / SharePoint integration, or a comparable enterprise document and collaboration stack. Real experience keeping cloud or AI usage costs under control: you know what drives the bill and how to attribute and cap it. A pragmatist's instinct for adopting over building where infrastructure is concerned - you'd rather configure something that exists than write something new - paired with a bias toward shipping when it comes to solutions. Clear communication. You can explain a trade-off to a fund manager and hold your own in a technical review with a central engineering team. Comfort with real ownership in a small team, where you set the working patterns rather than inherit them. Bonus Points For Full-stack or application development experience, particularly with Streamlit , FastAPI or HTMX. Familiarity with the Databricks ecosystem - Unity Catalog, Databricks Apps, Lakebase , Genie - or equivalent tooling. Experience with vector search, embeddings, document AI or retrieval-augmented generation in production. Experience with Terraform, GitHub Actions or similar, to keep configuration version-controlled and repeatable. FinOps experience: usage monitoring, budgets, showback and chargeback. Having supported analysts and non-specialist builders using a shared data environment. Experience in a regulated or audited setting such as financial services, infrastructure investment or energy. [ Read our Impact Report ] | [ See our Trustpilot ] The role ⚡ 📍 London (Hybrid) | 🤝 3 days in the office | 💰 Competitive Salary + Benefits This role sits in the Credit Risk team who are hugely influential to our overall lending process. They look at measuring our risk, optimising our credit risk funnel and forecasting the performance of our loan portfolios. To do this, they work with the credit risk modelling, engineering, data management, capital markets and business operations teams to truly understand our objectives and shape analytical solutions. Focusing on our Credit Risk lending capabilities, you’ll be given the opportunity to think outside the box and come up with a wide range of suggestions and ideas to optimise our ability to lend to small businesses, while also delivering strong returns for our investors. Primarily responsible for monitoring our Credit Strategy to identify useful trends and opportunities to optimise our lending strategy Involved with all aspects of credit strategy analytics, from loss rate forecasting to segmentation analysis Guiding business decisions by carrying out ad hoc analysis, providing credit risk insights and recommendations for optimising credit risk strategies and business processes Collaborate with experts from different functions, particularly Engineering and Operations, to ensure daily running of our lending business and to implement any Credit Strategy changes What we’re looking for 🌱 A degree in a highly numerical discipline (e.g., Mathematics, Statistics, Engineering, Computer Science, or Physical Sciences) Open to entry-level candidates and recent graduates. Ability to guide decisions through data—from defining the underlying business question to analyzing datasets and communicating actionable recommendations. Excellent communication skills, particularly with regards to translating data analyses and numbers into actionable insights tailored to the audience Intermediate-to-advanced Excel skills. title: Software Engineer, Regulatory Reporting
description: <p><span style="text-decoration: underline;"><strong>About Clear Street:</strong></span></p> <div>Clear Street’s mission is to give every sophisticated investor access to every asset, in every market, through a unified platform built for speed, transparency and scale.</div> <div><br>We give our clients the technology, tools, and service once reserved for the largest institutions, rebuilt with modern infrastructure. Our single, cloud-native, end-to-end capital markets platform powers investor growth today and is transforming how they can interact with markets tomorrow.<br><br></div> <div>For more information, visit <a href="https://clearstreet.io/" target="_blank" data-saferedirecturl="https://www.google.com/url?q=https://clearstreet.io&source=gmail&ust=1766243799031000&usg=AOvVaw2TBe5KeG89pR0V5dJX88v8">https://clearstreet.io</a>.</div> <p> </p> <p><strong>The Team:</strong></p> <p><br>The Regulatory Reporting Engineering team at Clear Street is a small team with a great deal of responsibility. We work closely with stakeholders to ensure that we meet all our financial and regulatory obligations in a timely fashion. Our goal is to make the lives of our stakeholders easier by leveraging innovative technology to create automated solutions for their workflows. As Clear Street grows into more product lines and geographical regions, every member of the team will have an opportunity to have an immense impact on the firm as a whole.  Join our team and be part of a dynamic environment where you can make a significant contribution, collaborate with talented professionals, and work with cutting-edge technology to drive operational excellence.</p> <p> </p> <p><strong>The Role:</strong></p> <p>As a Lead Software Engineer on the Regulatory Reporting Engineering team, you will play an integral role in automating our Compliance & Finance regulatory processes. You'll build on your analytical skills to create solutions that process large amounts of data from our data warehouse to generate clean, correct reporting, including building out reconciliations.</p> <p>You will partner with key stakeholders across the Compliance, Finance, and Treasury teams  to understand regulatory/financial obligations and business requirements, and translate them into clean designs and scalable solutions. As the tech lead in the team, you will provide technical guidance, prioritizing work, perform hands-on design and development and code review,  as well as evolve our technical standards and best practices.</p> <p> </p> <p><strong>Tech Stack:</strong> Python, SQL, Snowflake, Retool, Docker, Kubernetes, Argo, Metaplane, REST APIs</p> <p><strong>Required Qualifications: </strong></p> <ul> <li>You have at least three (3) years of software design and development experience including CI/CD, source code control, testing, and quality management.</li> <li>You are highly proficient in Python,  SQL, database design, and have experience working with data warehouses like Snowflake to generate complex solutions at scale.</li> <li>You are a self-starter with a sense of urgency and an eagerness to learn and explore new technologies as appropriate to solve business problems.</li> <li>You are a strong communicator who can interact in a clear and concise manner with non-technical business stakeholders, product managers as well engineers.</li> <li>You can troubleshoot and logically assess problems and determine solutions.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Bonus Qualifications:</strong></p> <ul> <li>You have experience working in the post-trade automation space designing and architecting systems that deliver solutions to complex data problems.</li> <li>You have experience generating complex financial industry regulatory reports like EMIR, MFID,  SFTR, CPR, K Factor etc.</li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><strong>We Offer:</strong></p> <p>At Clear Street, we offer competitive compensation packages, company equity, pension, gender neutral parental leave, and full medical and dental insurance. Our belief has always been that we are better as a business when we are all together in person. As such, we are requiring employees to be in the office a minimum of three days per week.</p> <p>Our top priority is our people. We’re continuously investing in a culture that promotes collaboration. We help each other through challenges and celebrate each other's successes. We believe that modern workplaces succeed by virtue of having high-performance workforces that are diverse — in ideas, in cultures, and in experiences. We put in the effort to make such a workplace a daily reality and are proud to be an equal opportunity employer.</p> <p> </p> <p>#LI-Hybrid</p> Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Applied AI Scientist, Simulation & Reinforcement Learning
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>At Locus Robotics, we build AI-powered systems and intelligent robots that keep global supply chains running. Our platform combines advanced AI, real-time decision-making, and autonomous robotics to help leading companies improve efficiency, scale operations, and adapt to constant change.</p> <p>Locus Robotics is a place to do meaningful work with real-world impact, where your ideas move quickly from concept to deployment. We invest in our people, encourage continuous learning, and give you the opportunity to grow your career while building technology that is used every day at global scale.</p></div><p>As an Applied AI Scientist, Simulation & Reinforcement Learning, you'll own the simulator behind SDL, our programme building a world-first, reinforcement-learning-driven orchestration framework for people and robots. That framework needs a simulator that is trustworthy enough to develop, tune and validate it before it touches a live warehouse.<br><br>You will take over day-to-day ownership of our discrete-event simulation (built on SimPy), make it measurably closer to reality, and use it as the training and evaluation ground for learning-based policies. Simulation comes first; reinforcement learning grows to be the larger part of the role as the simulator matures. You'll compare your simulations against live operational data from some of the world's largest fulfilment sites, and your work will decide what is validated and shipped to fleets of robots in customer sites worldwide.<br><br>This is not a notebook role. The simulator you own is the foundation that decides what ships to customer sites worldwide. You will work in a small, collaborative team where research meets production, as part of Applied Data Science (ADS), reporting to Oscar Mendez.</p> <ul> <li> <div> <div> <div> <div><strong>Location:</strong> This is a remote position based in the United Kingdom. Candidates must reside in the UK.</div> <div><strong>Right to Work:</strong> Candidates must have the legal right to work in the UK. Locus Robotics is unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position, now or in the future.</div> </div> </div> </div> </li> </ul> <p><strong>Responsibilities</strong><br><br>Own the simulator</p> <ul> <li>Own and develop our SimPy-based discrete-event simulator, including its logic, design choices and the fragile areas that need care.</li> <li>Pay down technical debt: improve test coverage, code quality, reproducibility and developer tooling.</li> <li>Build the experiment infrastructure around the simulator: orchestration, study management, reporting and automated runs across benchmark sites.</li> <li>Generate and maintain site data (e.g. distance files, configs) needed to simulate customer warehouses.</li> <li>Support scenario testing and sensitivity analysis for our order-engine and orchestration teams.</li> </ul> <p>Tune and close the sim2real gap</p> <ul> <li>Define, measure and reduce the sim-to-real gap against real site data.</li> <li>Run parameter optimisation and tuning studies (e.g. Optuna), and diagnose anomalies and non-determinism.</li> <li>Model warehouse processes such as congestion, picker behaviour and queueing at the right level of fidelity.</li> <li>Communicate results and confidence clearly to engineering, product and operations stakeholders.</li> <li>Use Optimization, RL & DL to tune the simulator</li> </ul> <p>Grow into reinforcement learning</p> <ul> <li>Turn the simulator into a proper RL environment (Gymnasium/Gym-style interfaces) with fast, repeatable, scalable training runs.</li> <li>Design, train and evaluate RL policies, starting with guidance generation, and benchmark them against current heuristic algorithms.</li> <li>Guard against overfitting to simulator artefacts, and design experiments that show what transfers to the real world.</li> <li>Prototype, evaluate and productionise learning-based components alongside the wider ML, MLOps and OE teams.</li> <li>Stay current with RL, multi-agent systems and simulation research, and assess what is applicable to Locus.</li> <li>Contribute to internal technical papers, patents and, where appropriate, publications.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Qualifications</strong></p> <ul> <li>A PhD in Computer Science, AI/ML, Robotics, Mathematics, Physics, Operations Research or a related quantitative field, or MSc and 5+ years of industry experience applying AI/ML or simulation to real-world problems.</li> <li>Hands-on experience building, extending or validating simulators, ideally discrete-event simulation (SimPy or similar).</li> <li>Practical experience with reinforcement learning and training simulation-based agents, including simulation for RL and Gym-style environments.</li> <li>Strong Python and software engineering fundamentals: testing, code review, maintainable and reproducible code.</li> <li>Rigorous experimental and statistical thinking: benchmarking, tuning, ablations, uncertainty.</li> <li>Experience in robotics, logistics, warehouse or other operations-heavy domains.</li> <li>Publications in major AI, ML, robotics or vision venues (e.g. NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, AAAI, RSS, CoRL, ICRA, IROS, CVPR, ICCV, ECCV).</li> <li>Excellent English communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to engage diverse audiences effectively and explain uncertain results clearly to technical and non-technical audiences in a multidisciplinary environment.</li> </ul> <p>The expected base salary range for this role i<strong>s</strong> GBP 70,000 - 120,000 <strong> </strong>based on external market data, plus bonus and equity. Actual offers will depend on factors such as the candidate's experience, education, training, key or critical skills, geographic location, and current market and business conditions.<br><br></p><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>Additional Information </strong></p> <p>Locus Robotics is an equal opportunity employer.</p> <p>Application Fraud Detection Notice: To help maintain a fair and secure hiring process, Locus Robotics may use AI-assisted and other automated tools to detect suspected fraud, misrepresentation, or misuse of the application process. Hiring decisions are not made solely by automated means unless otherwise disclosed where required by law. </p> <p>It is unlawful in Massachusetts to require or administer a lie detector test as a condition of employment or continued employment. An employer who violates this law shall be subject to criminal penalties and civil liability. </p> <p> </p></div> Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

reviews, routine performance data and other sources into prioritised, feasible improvements in clinical care, service delivery and wider health system capabilities.</li> <li>Guide multidisciplinary institutional capabilities, including decision-making processes, performance management, accountability mechanisms and continuous improvement practices.</li> <li>Design and guide practical implementation approaches, including change management plans, improvement processes, team-based coaching and mechanisms to address barriers to implementation.</li> <li>Promote government ownership and sustainability by embedding improved practices, management routines and accountability processes within existing health systems.</li> </ul> <h4><strong>Country Implementation and Technical delivery improvements, identifying emerging challenges, and recommending course corrections.</li> <li>Work closely with country teams, government counterparts and implementing partners to identify priorities, address operational challenges and support effective programme delivery.</li> <li>Provide technical leadership on country assessments, programme design and implementation planning, implementation learning, and performance measurement to assess the effectiveness of service delivery changes, identify emerging challenges, and inform course correction.</li> <li>Document and experience in clinical service delivery, health systems strengthening and service delivery transformation, including substantial experience in low- and middle-income countries.</li> <li>Demonstrated Translate complex analysis into clear recommendations for Product, Commercial, and senior leadership. What we're looking for... Ideally, 5+ years of experience in product analytics, growth analytics, marketplace analytics, retail media analytics, performance marketing analytics, data science, or a closely adjacent role. Strong commercial judgement and fluency in ROAS, CPA, incrementality, attribution, LTV, conversion, margin, and marketplace trade-offs. Deep data skills. Rigorous experimentation experience. You can design clean A/B tests, reason about incrementality and power, interpret results honestly, and know when data is good enough to act on. Experience analysing digital funnels, browsing behaviour, search behaviour, clickouts, conversion, paid placements, shopping discovery, or marketplace dynamics. Experience with segmentation, targeting, personalisation, recommendation systems, ranking, marketplace allocation, retail media, or paid media measurement would be highly valuable. Strong product instincts, with the ability to recommend and evaluate shopping features that improve customer engagement, discovery, conversion, and monetisation. Commercially minded and comfortable working across Product and Sales. You can understand both customer value and merchant performance, and translate analysis into decisions that improve both. Strong communicator who can explain complex analytical concepts clearly to Product, Commercial, and Executive stakeholders. description: About Infrata Infrata, part of dss+, is a specialist infrastructure advisory business of around 100 people working with investors, lenders, owners, operators and governments across transport, aviation, maritime, energy, digital infrastructure and the energy transition. We are looking for someone who can help us build on these strengths by developing new consulting services, winning work and leading projects. You will work with our technical specialists to identify where clients need advice beyond due diligence, develop services we are well placed to deliver, and take them to clients. You will also lead the projects you win, bringing in specialists as needed. Your impact at Infrata The role has three main responsibilities: developing services, winning work and leading delivery. Develop services. Work with clients and colleagues to identify problems we have the expertise to address but do not currently advise on. Develop services we can deliver consistently, with a clear scope, team, price and evidence of their value. Win work. Introduce these services to existing and new clients, lead proposals and presentations, and secure new projects. Lead delivery. Lead the projects you win, agreeing the approach, managing the client relationship and team, and taking responsibility for the quality of the advice. Our due diligence specialists will contribute their expertise; you will be responsible for the overall engagement. Test ideas with clients before investing in their development, and focus on those with genuine demand. Define the client need, approach, team, fees and deliverables for each service, supported by evidence of our experience. Build the supporting material: credentials, case studies, proposal templates, pitch decks. Build and maintain relationships with decision-makers at investors, lenders, operators and public bodies. Identify opportunities, qualify them, and write or lead proposals and pitches. Work with sector leads to extend existing due diligence relationships into advisory work. Keep the pipeline and client records in our systems current. Engagement leadership Act as lead consultant on engagements you win: scope, plan, staff, budget, and deliver. Define the questions the project needs to answer and the analysis required. Take responsibility for the conclusions and final recommendations. Manage the client relationship day to day, including scope changes, difficult messages and sign-off. Run the project team, including specialists drawn from across Infrata and dss+, and give them clear briefs and feedback. Deliver high-quality work on time and within budget, building client confidence and opportunities for further work. Building the team's consulting capability Coach due diligence staff who work on your engagements in consulting skills: problem structuring, client handling, writing for decision-makers, presenting. Set clear standards for strategic advisory proposals, workplans and deliverables, and apply them in your own work. Strategy You will advise owners, operators, developers and public bodies on areas including market entry and growth strategy, asset and portfolio strategy, business planning, governance and assurance, policy and regulatory positioning, and investment case development. Value creation Working primarily with private equity and infrastructure fund investors and their portfolio companies, you will lead engagements such as full-potential reviews, 100-day plans, operational and commercial improvement programmes, exit readiness and portfolio performance reviews. Climate advisory You will support investors, lenders and operators with decarbonisation roadmaps, climate risk and resilience assessments, transition planning, sustainability strategy, and ESG and climate reporting. Data and digital services You will help investors, lenders, operators and public bodies get greater value from data. This could include turning existing traffic, asset, transaction and benchmark data into advisory products or subscription services, using AI tools to accelerate analysis and delivery, and helping clients make better use of their own data. Most projects will combine Infrata's knowledge of aviation, maritime, roads, rail, energy and digital infrastructure with dss+ expertise in operations, safety and sustainability. A background in project finance, lender's or investor's technical advisory, or assurance would help you understand our clients' needs and how our team works. Experience leading strategy, value creation or climate advisory projects, with responsibility for the engagement rather than an individual part of the work. Direct experience of winning work: writing proposals, pitching, negotiating scope and fees, and converting relationships into revenue.
